newsitem.title: USA: Newspaper shrs rise as fears on paper prices ease.
newsitem.headline: Newspaper shrs rise as fears on paper prices ease.

text.p: Newspaper stocks were broadly higher in early afternoon trading, with investors hopeful that advertising revenues would stay strong, and less worried that newsprint prices would rise, analysts said.
"The group is up," said Bill Bird, an analyst at Smith Barney. "It's more a function of the stocks having sold off last week. They've recovered a bit."
Gannett jumped 2-3/4 to 100-3/4, A.H. Belo Corp gained 5/16 to 46-1/16, Tribune Co added 5/16 to 52-3/16, McClatchy Newspapers Inc rose 5/16 to 33-15/16.
Also, Washington Post Co was up 6-4/16 to 423-7/16.

The higher stock prices reflect investor confidence that newsprint prices are not going to crimp profits. While some analysts said newsprint prices were not likely to rise again this year, others contended that prices almost always rise in an advertising recovery.
Newspaper stocks had been weak since mid-July, on concern that newsprint prices would jump, said J. Kendrick Noble, a media consultant.
There is also bullishness about the state of the industry, after strong second-quarter results.

"There's growing confidence that corporate profits will look good in the second half," Bird said. "The group is still attractive to a lot of people, who believe that earnings growth will likely outpace the S&P 500 for another quarter, if not longer."

Analysts said newspapers continue to see above-average ad revenue growth. The newspaper industry is posting some "pretty good advertising" revenues so far in the third quarter, said Charles Baker at Salomon Brothers. "People were worried that ad revenues would slow down."

Earlier Wednesday, Gannett announced it bought New Jersey Press Inc, which publishes the Asbury Park Press and Home News & Tribune in East Brunswick. Terms were not disclosed. Analysts did not attribute the stock jump to the deal.
